narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. As a result, the company has decided to deny your promotion.

The prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. First, your overall work experience of 1-5 years across all jobs was the strongest influence, pulling the prediction toward you staying because this range matches half of the employees the model expects to remain. However, this positive signal was outweighed by the second most important factor: you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities strongly pushed the model toward expecting you to leave. Third, the fact that you do not have medical insurance in your current role also nudged the prediction slightly toward departure, as most employees the model predicts will stay do receive coverage.

Taken together, your relatively short total experience helps the model see some stability, but the presence of outside offers and lack of medical benefits tipped the balance enough to forecast that you are likely to move on.

The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as exploring promotion paths, offering competitive benefits, or addressing any concerns raised by external opportunities. You may wish to clarify your career intentions so both sides can make informed decisions. (218 words)
